lines.about: The Blue Line is the longest corridor of the Delhi Metro at 56.6 km with over 50 stations. It has two branches — the main line from Dwarka Sector 21 to Noida Electronic City, and a branch from Yamuna Bank to Vaishali. It connects West Delhi (Dwarka, Janakpuri) to East Delhi (Laxmi Nagar, Anand Vihar) and into Noida and Ghaziabad.

The Green Line runs 29.6 km from Brigadier Hoshiyar Singh station in Bahadurgarh (Haryana) through West Delhi to Inderlok and Kirti Nagar. It has two branches — the main corridor from Bahadurgarh to Kirti Nagar, and a short branch from Ashok Park Main to Inderlok. It serves the industrial and residential belts of Mundka, Nangloi, and Paschim Vihar.

The Grey Line is the shortest corridor on the Delhi Metro network, running just 4.3 km with 4 stations from Dhansa Bus Stand to Dwarka. It connects the Najafgarh area of Southwest Delhi to the main Blue Line network at Dwarka, providing metro connectivity to a previously underserved region.

The Magenta Line runs 38.2 km from Janakpuri West in West Delhi to Botanical Garden in Noida, passing through IGI Airport Terminal 1, South Delhi, and the Okhla corridor. It provides a direct metro connection to Terminal 1 of the airport and connects areas like Hauz Khas, Panchsheel Park, and Kalkaji. A northern branch connects from Janakpuri West to Majlis Park via Rohini.

The Pink Line is a 59.6 km semi-circular corridor with 38 stations, making it one of the longest single lines. It loops around Delhi from Majlis Park in the north, through West Delhi (Rajouri Garden), South Delhi (INA, Lajpat Nagar), East Delhi (Anand Vihar), and up to Shiv Vihar in Northeast Delhi. A second branch runs from Majlis Park through Burari to Maujpur–Babarpur.

The Red Line was Delhi Metro's first line — it's been running since 2002. Goes 34 km from Rithala in the northwest all the way to Shaheed Sthal in Ghaziabad, crossing the Yamuna into East Delhi. About 4 lakh people ride it every day, mostly between Kashmere Gate and the Shahdara/Dilshad Garden belt.

The Violet Line stretches 46.6 km from Kashmere Gate in Old Delhi southward through Central Delhi and into Faridabad, terminating at Raja Nahar Singh (Ballabhgarh). It connects landmarks like ITO, Khan Market, Nehru Place, and covers the entire Faridabad corridor. It is the second-longest line after the Blue Line.

The Yellow Line is the busiest corridor of the Delhi Metro, spanning 49.3 km from Samaypur Badli in North Delhi to Millennium City Centre in Gurugram. It passes through the heart of the city — Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi Railway Station, and AIIMS — carrying over 12 lakh passengers daily, making it the most used rapid transit line in India.
